note: Replay timelines for scripts/autoscan-timing.test.mjs. Virtual milliseconds. `screen` is what is actually displayed; `reads` optionally overrides what the local observer reports for a given observation index range, modelling read noise. No screen is captured and no service is called.

costs.note: A MODEL, calibrated from measured native costs. Not measurements in themselves: each side is a flat per-observation figure standing in for a range, and the harness picks one of two values per observation. Calibration source: the parent probed an actual selected game window, local only, 16 samples (capture 125-150ms, LiveText 90-115ms warm, eager PNG 144-153ms, total 370-405ms every probe; cold 750ms). `old` models that pipeline at a flat 400ms. `new` models it with eager PNG removed from observations and identical-image observer reads cached natively, so an unchanged frame costs the capture alone (150ms, observation 0ms) and a changed one costs 250ms. recognizeMs 900 is an ASSUMPTION for the simulation, not a measurement: observed endpoint times in existing logs ranged roughly 450-1569ms, so any single figure understates the spread and latency results scale with it.

fingerprint: The harness supplies contentFingerprint from the displayed screen content, standing in for the native exact RGBA digest. It is deliberately independent of observer read noise: the digest describes pixels, the reading describes what an engine made of them.
